name: FL-17
label: Likely R

key_factors: Republican-leaning district (R+10 PVI) with incumbent Greg Steube running
Steube holds a large financial advantage: $2.1M cash vs. $24K for Montavon
Prediction markets price Steube around 95% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Steube: a Republican-leaning seat, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage over a little-funded challenger. Markets price the race similarly, so the forecast stays near the baseline with no evidence to move it.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending targeting Steube would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Greg Steube seeks another term in a southwest Florida district that leans about ten points Republican at the presidential level. He enters the general election with the advantages of incumbency and a dominant fundraising position, holding roughly $2.1 million on hand against about $24,000 for Democrat Matthew Montavon, with an independent candidate also on the ballot but minimally funded.

No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Steube roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. The forecast therefore expects a comfortable Republican victory, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific evidence of a contest.
